341632.title: Lyngsø and Pedersen's antipalindromic subsequence conjecture
341632.statement:
A **binary word** is a word over the alphabet $\{0,1\}$; a **circular word** is an equivalence class of linear words under rotations; an **antipalindrome** is a binary word whose letters in opposite positions are distinct. A subsequence of a circular word is a subsequence of one of its linear representations.

**Lyngsø and Pedersen's conjecture.** Every binary circular word of length $n$ divisible by $6$ with equal numbers of zeros and ones has an antipalindromic subsequence of length at least

$$
\frac{2}{3}n.
$$

The conjecture arose from an approximation algorithm for a two-dimensional protein-folding problem. The source reports no progress toward a proof; the bound $\frac{1}{2}n$ is known, but no better bound is proved.

341634.title: Weak palindromic subsequence conjecture for binary circular words
341634.statement:
A **binary circular word** is a circular word over the alphabet $\{0,1\}$, and a palindromic subsequence reads identically from both ends.

**Weak circular-palindrome conjecture.** Every binary circular word of length $n$ has a palindromic subsequence of length at least

$$
\frac{2}{3}n.
$$

The source presents this as the palindromic counterpart of the antipalindromic conjectures. A bound of $\frac12n$ is immediate, and no better bound is known to be proved.

341665.title: Zero-sum partition conjecture for finite Abelian groups with multiple involutions
341665.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite Abelian group of order $n$ with more than one involution. Let

$$
n-1=r_1+r_2+\cdots+r_t
$$

be a partition of $n-1$ with $r_i\geq 3$ for $1\leq i\leq t$, where $t$ is any positive integer. **Zero-sum partition conjecture.** There is a partition of $\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$ into pairwise disjoint subsets $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_t$ such that

$$
|A_i|=r_i\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{a\in A_i}a=0
$$

for $1\leq i\leq t$. The conjecture is true for groups isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^m$, as proved by Egawa; the parser marks this candidate as resolved, although the supplied context does not state whether the full assertion or only that special case has been resolved.

341678.title: The chromatic splitting conjecture for the zero-line of the descent spectral sequence
341678.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $n$ a height, $E_n$ Morava $E$-theory, and $\mathbb{G}_n$ the Morava stabilizer group. Consider the descent spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{s,t}\cong H_c^s(\mathbb{G}_n,(E_n)_t)\Longrightarrow\pi_{t-s}L_{K(n)}S^0.
$$

**Zero-line chromatic splitting conjecture.** If $p$ is odd, or if $p=2$ and $n$ is odd, then

$$
E_\infty^{*,0}\cong\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\subseteq\pi_*L_{K(n)}S^0;
$$

for $e_i$ detected by a multiple of $x_i$. If $p=2$ and $n$ is even, then

$$
E_\infty^{*,0}\cong\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(f,e_1,\ldots,e_n)/(2f,e_nf)\subseteq\pi_*L_{K(n)}S^0,
$$

where $f$ is detected by $\widetilde{\chi}_n$. These phenomena have been observed at heights $n\leq2$; the source presents the general assertion as conjectural.

341693.title: Three-candidate conjecture for 3-graphs with bounded union
341693.statement:
Let ${\mathcal F}\subset {[n]\choose3}$ be a 3-graph. It has property $U(s,2s+1)$ if every choice of $F_1,\ldots,F_s\in{\mathcal F}$ satisfies

$$
|F_1\cup\cdots\cup F_s|\le2s+1.
$$

Define the three candidate families

$$
{\mathcal F}_1={\mathcal A}(1,1,n,3),\qquad {\mathcal F}_2={\mathcal A}(s+1,2,n,3),\qquad {\mathcal F}_3={\mathcal A}(2s+1,3,n,3).
$$

**Three-candidate conjecture.** If ${\mathcal F}$ has property $U(s,2s+1)$, then

$$
|{\mathcal F}|\le\max_{i\in[3]}|{\mathcal F}_i|.
$$

All three displayed families have property $U(s,2s+1)$; the conjecture concerns the first case for $k=3$ not covered by the preceding general results. The paper notes that this case can have three potential extremal families rather than two, and its status is open.

341733.title: Bressoud's generalized Borwein conjecture
341733.statement:
Suppose that $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive rational numbers, and $K$ is a positive integer such that $\alpha K$ and $\beta K$ are integers. If

$$
1\leq\alpha+\beta\leq2K+1
$$

with strict inequalities if $K=2$, and

$$
\beta-K\leq n-m\leq K-\alpha,
$$

then the polynomial

$$
\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}(-1)^jq^{j(K(\alpha+\beta)j+K(\alpha-\beta))/2}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{m+n}{m+Kj}_q
$$

has non-negative coefficients. Bressoud's conjecture generalizes the Borwein setting through rational parameters and restricted hook-difference-type $q$-binomial sums. The supplied text gives no resolution.

348689.title: Uniqueness conjecture for optimal surveillance strategies on directed line graphs
348689.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}=(V,\mathcal{E})$ be a directed line graph with $n\geq 3$ nodes, and consider Problem~, which seeks an optimal surveillance strategy for the graph. **Uniqueness of the optimal strategy.** The optimal solution to Problem~ is unique. The paper introduces this conjecture to establish its main result for directed line graphs, in the nontrivial attack-duration range $n-1\leq\tau\leq 2n-3$; no resolution is supplied in the given text.

348734.title: Boyer et al.'s sphere-of-influence dimension conjecture
348734.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with no isolated vertices. Its **SIG-dimension**, denoted by $SIG(G)$, is the least integer $d$ such that $G$ can be realized as a sphere-of-influence graph in $\mathbb{R}^d$ equipped with the sup-norm.

**Boyer et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
SIG(G)\leq \left\lceil\frac{2n}{3}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture gives a general upper bound for the dimension needed to realize graphs as sphere-of-influence graphs. The paper reports the almost-matching bound $SIG(G)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{2n}{3}\right\rfloor+2$, but does not establish the conjectured inequality itself.

348828.title: Sticky Matroid Conjecture
348828.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid. It is **sticky** if, for any two matroids $N_1$ and $N_2$ with $E(M)=E(N_1)\cap E(N_2)$ and $M=N_1|_{E(M)}=N_2|_{E(M)}$, there exists an amalgam of $N_1$ and $N_2$. A matroid is **modular** when every pair of flats is modular. **Sticky Matroid Conjecture.** Every sticky matroid is modular. This is the converse of the known fact that every modular matroid is sticky. The paper relates this conjecture to the hypermodular matroid conjecture and Kantor's conjecture.

348952.title: The matching-deletability conjecture for 3-edge-connected graphs
348952.statement: Let $G$ be a $3$-edge-connected graph. A **matching** is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, and a **3-edge-cut** is an edge cut of size three. A matching is **deletable** when all its edges can become deletable in one orientation, as defined in the paper. **Matching-deletability conjecture.** If $M$ is a matching of $G$ intersecting each $3$-edge-cut of $G$ in at most one edge, then $M$ is deletable. This proposed generalization is presented as a possible route toward improving the Frank-number bound; its status is open in the supplied text.

349006.title: Strong Pólya–Szegő conjecture for finite spectral determination of regular polygons
349006.statement: Let $n\geq 3$, let $\Omega$ be a convex $n$-gon, and let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Write $\lambda_i(\Omega)$ for the $i$th eigenvalue of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, and let $N=N(n)$ be the integer from Theorem 3. **Strong Pólya–Szegő conjecture.** The number $N=N(n)$ in Theorem 3 may be taken equal to $1$; equivalently, if the first eigenvalue of a convex $n$-gon coincides with that of a regular $n$-gon, then the convex $n$-gon is congruent to that regular $n$-gon. The preceding theorem establishes finite spectral determination for some $N(n)$ without an area-normalization assumption. The conjecture strengthens the area-constrained Pólya–Szegő conjecture, and the source gives no resolution.

349096.title: Characterization of equality in the mixed metric dimension bound
349096.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $c(G)$ be its cyclomatic number, let $L_1(G)$ be its number of leaves, and let $\mathrm{mdim}(G)$ be its mixed metric dimension. A **cactus graph** is a graph in which all cycles are pairwise edge disjoint; a **balanced Theta graph** is the class of Theta graphs defined as balanced in the paper. **Equality characterization conjecture.** 
$$
\mathrm{mdim}(G)=L_1(G)+2c(G)
$$
 if and only if $G$ is a cactus graph in which every cycle has precisely one vertex of degree at least $3$, or $G$ is a balanced Theta graph. This conjecture refines the general upper-bound conjecture by characterizing exactly when equality occurs; the paper establishes the claimed equality for the listed families but leaves the converse classification open.

349110.title: The 6-color conjecture for signed triangular grids
349110.statement:
A **signed graph** is a graph whose edges are assigned positive or negative signs; its chromatic number is the least order of a signed target graph admitting a signed graph homomorphism. A **signed triangular grid** is a finite induced subgraph of the graph associated with the tiling of the plane by equilateral triangles.

**Signed triangular-grid chromatic-number conjecture.** The chromatic number of every signed triangular grid is $6$.

The paper gives a construction showing that signed triangular grids in which every $C_4$ is unbalanced can be colored with $6$ colors, making this extremal case particularly relevant. The conjecture concerns the exact chromatic number of all signed triangular grids and is not resolved in the supplied text.

350309.title: The Catalan-square conjecture for connected chordal diagrams
350309.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_{n}(T_{\geqslant 4},B_{\geqslant 4})$ be the set of connected chord diagrams of size $n$ avoiding top and bottom cycles of size at least $4$, and let $C_n$ denote the $n$th Catalan number. **The Catalan-square conjecture.** The cardinality of this set is

$$
\left|\mathcal{C}_{n}(T_{\geqslant 4},B_{\geqslant 4})\right|=C_n^2.
$$

The claim is one of several experimentally suggested enumerations for forbidden-subdiagram classes; it is stated as open in the source.

352284.title: Stanchescu's difference-set lower-bound conjecture in Euclidean space
352284.statement:
Let $d \geq 2$ and let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set with affine dimension $\dim(A)=d$. **Stanchescu's conjecture.** Then

$$
|A-A| \geq \left(2d-2+\frac{1}{d-1}\right)|A|-(2d^2-4d+3).
$$

This conjecture proposes that Stanchescu's construction from $2d-2$ parallel arithmetic progressions gives the best possible lower bound for the size of the difference set of a full-dimensional finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The bound is known in dimensions $d=1$, $d=2$, and $d=3$, while the higher-dimensional cases were presented as open in the source.

373826.title: Gastineau–Togni conjecture on packing colorings of subcubic graphs
373826.statement: A packing $(1,1,2,3)$-coloring is a partition of the vertex set into four classes whose pairwise vertex distances are respectively at least $2$, $2$, $3$, and $4$. **Gastineau–Togni conjecture.** Every connected subcubic graph except the Petersen graph is packing $(1,1,2,3)$-colorable. The paper says that this was posed as a conjecture because the authors believe it is true; no resolution is supplied in the candidate context.

374986.title: Vergara's conjecture for graphs with independence number two
374986.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with independence number $\alpha(G)=2$, let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number, and let $K_{\chi(G)}$ be the complete graph on $\chi(G)$ vertices. A **weak immersion** of a graph $H$ in $G$ consists of an injection from $V(H)$ to $V(G)$ and pairwise edge-disjoint paths in $G$ representing the edges of $H$. **Vergara's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ contains a weak immersion of $K_{\chi(G)}$. The source presents this as the Abu-Khzam–Langston conjecture restricted to graphs of independence number two and notes its equivalence, for graphs with $\alpha(G)\leq 2$, to the corresponding assertion involving $K_{\lceil |V(G)|/2\rceil}$. The status of this named formulation is not separately established in the supplied text.

381517.title: The rank-+1 hypergraph conjecture for quantum entropy inequalities
381517.statement:
Let an $n$-party inequality of the form defined in the source be given, and let an $m$-graph be a hypergraph whose edges have size at most $m$. The inequality **contracts** on a class of hypergraphs if its contraction map sends every hypergraph in that class to a hypergraph satisfying the inequality.

**Rank-$n+1$ hypergraph conjecture.** If an $n$-party inequality contracts on $(n+1)$-graphs, then it is a valid inequality on all hypergraphs of finite rank.

This conjecture formalizes the expectation that, after including the purifier, no entanglement structure involving more than $n+1$ indivisible subsystems contributes new information to an $n$-party entropy inequality. Its status is not determined by the supplied text.

381581.title: Polynomial codegrees and dual defects of general determinantal loci
381581.statement:
Let $D^{s,n}_{n^2-m}$ denote the determinantal locus of general $n\times n$ matrices of the indicated rank parameter. For any fixed $m>0$, **the general determinantal-locus conjecture.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{the dual defect of }D^{s,n}_{n^2-m}\text{ is }\max(0,s^2-m),\text{ independently of }n,\\
&\text{and the codegree of }D^{s,n}_{n^2-m}\text{ depends polynomially on }n.
\end{aligned}
$$

The conjecture extends the known case $m=1$, where the dual defect is $s^2-1$ and the codegree is given by a polynomial expression in $n$. It predicts uniform behavior for defective general determinantal loci with fixed $m$; the source gives no resolution.

381582.title: Polynomial codegrees and dual defects of skew-symmetric determinantal loci
381582.statement:
Let $AD^{2s,2n}_{\binom{2n}{2}-m}$ denote the skew-symmetric determinantal locus in even dimension with the indicated rank parameter. For any fixed $m>0$, **the even skew-symmetric determinantal-locus conjecture.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{the dual defect of }AD^{2s,2n}_{\binom{2n}{2}-m}\text{ is }\max\left(0,\binom{2n}{2}-m\right),\text{ independently of }n,\\
&\text{and the codegree of }AD^{2s,2n}_{\binom{2n}{2}-m}\text{ depends polynomially on }n.
\end{aligned}
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the known case $m=1$, whose codegree is polynomial in $n$ and whose dual defect is $\binom{2s}{2}-1$. The source also suggests an analogous statement in odd dimensions, but does not formulate it as a separate conjecture; no resolution is given.
